checks: Same parity keeps all replacement product midpoints at integer bases in P. Pair-average comparisons fix the shared input tangent space. Any on-support tuple is tight for the actual target comparison, which supplies positive target mass and the unique actual affine offset.

The shared envelope is applied to the positive affine interpolant on the individual endpoint segment, giving midpoint denominator V. This is legitimate despite the concavity of the original L. Multiplication by (V/L(b))^d recovers the exact actual density at b. For d=1 the common endpoint atom masses and H(b)≥(H_-+H_+)/2 give the minimum bound directly.

At a contact midpoint the active affine roof plane has nonnegative gaps at the endpoints with sum zero. The two restricted supports are in its closed cell. Any recoupling of those marginals remains in contact and in the same parity. Therefore each restriction of the existing optimum is an unrestricted optimum. The actual output pieces stay disjoint at ties and are never rebuilt.

The inverse maps are locally Lipschitz on each tangent slice. Splitting by the finitely many input levels makes intrinsic null images null for the respective endpoint laws. The area formula with nonnegative Borel endpoint ceilings gives f≤F_i(T_i)|det DT_i| even without injectivity. Inner regularity applies on the Borel output strata.

At density-one points, the constant level coordinates have zero derivatives and the average tangent derivative is I. For q_i=(1/2)∇φ on the physical output slice, the gradient pullback identifies the symmetric positive semidefinite matrix (1/2)H DT_i, with common positive definite tangent Hessian H. Thus H^(1/2) DT_i H^(−1/2) is positive semidefinite, and averaged determinant roots are at most one by the trace inequality. This gives the harmonic-density bound at the unique reconstructed tuple. For an atom the same inverse maps give one tuple and its mass is bounded by each endpoint atom.

The discounted pushforward in each output part evaluates the discount at the reconstructed tuple. Its upper bound is the restriction of one target measure to that same part, and summing parts does not multiply the target by the number of roof planes.

The discounted inequality is weakly closed because b and a are continuous on the compact tuple range and domination is tested against nonnegative continuous functions. Separation from the nonnegative orthant and compact finite intersection turn the individual convex-test comparisons into one law satisfying all tests.

The physical Borel contact discrepancy is continuous at fixed normal on the finite-base product. Conditional domination, contact and convex order admit countably many determining tests. Summing classes multiplies the capacity by at most 2^n but does not multiply the logarithmic error, because the companion's bound is a concave homogeneous perspective. Old L-contact is preserved by the fixed endpoint integral and convex order for −L.

Independently checked the cube example. The second moment deficit is one quarter of the mean squared distance between endpoints. Convex-order improvement over the diagonal forces that deficit to zero. With endpoint L=1 and midpoint L=1+s the capacity equals (1+s)^(−d) times the midpoint law, Δ_0=m log(1+s), c_p=m, and T_p=T_{p,0}=m(1+s)^p. These are the claimed nonlinear equalities.

overlap.comparison: Has the same unweighted actual support and parity repair, but does not establish capacity for tuple-dependent a^d under a varying concave projective denominator.

Its actual planar edge example has the same (1+s)^2 capacity loss under a contact maximum. The present statement proves exact discounted repair in general and uniqueness of the improving cube pairing plus nonlinear equality.

Uses a supplied discounted branch ceiling as a hypothesis in rebuilding a surface martingale. It does not construct that one-copy discounted coupling. The new theorem gives the construction under a positive finite concave minimum.

readability: The symbol H_+ in the displayed midpoint density denotes the positive part at the output. Endpoint H values in that paragraph are the strictly positive numerator values on the positive input supports. The Hessian in the area argument is the restriction to the common tangent directions.
review_method: Independent mathematical proof review of the frozen normalized candidate
summary: Every strong-surplus optimizer on actual support contact satisfies the one-copy tuple-discount bound. Weak compactness and Borel selection retain one such bound with full convex order, and the entropy theorem gives the sharp nonlinear payment.
